description: Our team (BRAVEN) is making a moon base simulator using GANDI IDE. We are looking to help children understand what astronauts will pass when building and maintaining a lunar base.
summary: [What we built] We developed BRAVEN – Survival on the Moon, an interactive lunar expedition simulator designed for children aged 7 to 12 to experience managing an off-world colony. [How it answers the challenge] It directly addresses the challenge by transforming complex lunar survival concepts and authentic space data into intuitive, hands-on decision scenarios where young players balance vital resources like oxygen, energy, and scientific research. [Why it matters] This project is vital because it fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and STEM curiosity, empowering the Artemis generation to realize that a sustainable human presence on the Moon is achievable through thoughtful planning.
details:
Our project empowers children to manage a simulated lunar base through an interactive, event-driven Python application deployed via Streamlit. By processing player decisions in real time, the simulator calculates immediate consequences on base survival and resource stability. Incorporating authentic lunar conditions and data, the game fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, and scientific curiosity in young learners—equipping the next generation with the foundational skills to envision and support future space exploration.

To build this project, we leveraged state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence within Google Antigravity—utilizing advanced models such as Gemini 3.8 Flash and GPT-OSS 120B for development and problem-solving—alongside HeyGen for dynamic avatar video generation and Streamlit for an accessible web experience. Our creativity lies in bridging complex NASA telemetry and educational gaming: through intuitive mechanics, immersive audio-visual assets, and engaging storylines, we transform raw space science into an inspiring, hands-on learning adventure.
